text:
Alex: FYI a customer hit our embeddings endpoint with a mixed-dimension batch and got a 400. We currently require uniform dims, but they want a single request with 3x1536 + 2x768 vectors. Can we discuss options for accepting/handling mixed dims?

Priya: We intentionally required uniform dims because it makes batching and memory accounting predictable. Accepting mixed dims server-side means we'll have to split into sub-batches by dim, which increases request bookkeeping and could explode scheduler load.

Marco: Splitting server-side is feasible, but we need to be careful about quota/rate-limit semantics. If one client request becomes N internal requests, do we charge per original vector or per internal sub-request? We should tie billing to the original request to avoid double-charging. Also impacts throttling: one large original request shouldn't bump them past rate limits after splitting.

Jamie: From a console/telemetry perspective we should emit a single trace that includes sub-batch operations and a top-level "parent_request_id" so UI can show the end-to-end latency and the split breakdown. Add metrics: split_count, sub_batches, and per-dim histogram so support can quickly see payload shape.

Hana: Implementation idea: do the dim split as early as possible (edge/router) rather than inside the runtime hot path so we keep continuous-batching effectiveness on each dim. Router can produce M scheduling units with the same parent id and preferred scheduling window. Proposed header for incoming requests: `X-Embed-VecDims: 1536,1536,1536,768,768` (comma-separated). Router will parse, group indices, and forward compact sub-batches to the scheduler.

Priya: Agree on parent_request_id. Also we need to decide billing model: right now we bill per vector generation call (flat). If dims vary significantly, cost should reflect compute proportional to dim (roughly linear w/ dim for dense kernels). Suggest we bill as sum(dim) * base_unit so customers with mixed dims pay proportionally. That means we need to surface per-request cost estimate in the console before accepting.

Marco: If we change billing semantics we'll need a migration plan. For short-term, keep billing flat to avoid surprise, but add telemetry to retroactively compute dim-weighted cost so we can produce reports. Long-term: opt-in dim-weighted billing for enterprise customers.

Jamie: UI notes: add a new column in the per-route dashboard "effective_vector_ops" and a toggle to show raw vs normalized charges. Also add an alert rule when split_count > 1 for a request pattern (likely indicates client not batching correctly).

Hana: One more runtime concern: splitting reduces the opportunity for large cross-request batching. If many clients send mixed dims, each dim group's batch sizes shrink and p95 can regress. We should run a perf experiment in staging: simulate mixed-dim traffic at production-like QPS and measure p50/p95 and GPU occupancy. If occupancy drops, consider a background coalescer that pads smaller dims to match a common quantized bucket to increase batchability (with CPU mem tradeoffs).

ops-bot: deploy: started rollout "embed-mixed-dims-splitter" to staging (57% traffic) by hana — see deploy link: https://deploys.internal/release/4231 :rocket:

Alex: TL;DR / next steps: 1) Spec API header `X-Embed-VecDims` + `parent_request_id` (Hana) 2) Telemetry: add split_count, per-dim hist, parent trace linking (Marco + Jamie) 3) Billing: Priya to propose short-term vs long-term plan, include console cost preview 4) Perf tests in staging and report p50/p95/GPU occupancy (Hana) 5) Add support doc + deprecation notice if we later require uniform dims. I'll open a tracking ticket and assign tasks. @Priya @Marco @Hana please ack.
